case_name: Municipal Council, Samrala v Raj Kumar
respondent:
Raj Kumar
Supreme Court of India

6 January 2006
C.As. Nos. 299-300 of 2006 (Arising out of S.L.Ps. (C) Nos. 25488-89 of 2004)
The Order of the Court was as follows:
Leave granted.

facts: On or about 12-7-1994, an agenda of a meeting was placed before the Municipal Executive Council being Agenda No. 143
The said proposal came to be accepted by the Executive Council.
Pursuant thereto the respondent herein was appointed as a clerk on contract basis on a monthly salary of Rs 1000.
His services were dispensed with by an order dated 22-5-1997.
An industrial dispute having been raised, the matter was referred to the Labour Court, Ludhiana.

The learned Presiding Judge, Labour Court came to the conclusion that: 'It has been established that in the first spell, the workman worked from 24-6-1994 to 2-3-1996 and again from 7-3-1997 to 21-5-1997 and his services having been terminated vide office order Ext. M-5, he had worked for more than 240 days in the last calendar year, prior to termination of his services.'

The learned Presiding Judge, Labour Court in terms of his award dated 11-2-2003, on a finding that the said order of termination of the respondent was in violation of the provisions of Section 25-F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 directed that he be reinstated in service with 25% back wages.
The appellant herein filed a writ petition before the High Court of Punjab and Haryana, which by reason of the impugned judgment has been dismissed.
issues: Whether the respondent having been appointed on a contract basis, Section 25-F of the Industrial Disputes Act will have no application in the facts and circumstances of this case.
petitioner_arguments: Having regard to the provisions contained in S. 2(oo)(bb) of the Industrial Disputes Act, the respondent having been appointed for a fixed period on contract basis, Section 25-F of the Act will have no application in the facts and circumstances of this case.
respondent_arguments: The terms and conditions of appointment of the respondent nowhere suggest that the same was in relation to either in respect of a project or for a fixed period, and in that view of the matter the provisions of S. 2(oo)(bb) of the Act would have no application in the instant case.
court_reasoning: The learned Presiding Officer of the Labour Court as also the High Court arrived at their respective findings upon taking into consideration the first part of S. 2(oo)(bb) and not the second part thereof.
This Court was concerned with a different fact situation obtaining therein.
The termination of service of a workman engaged in a scheme or project may not amount to retrenchment within the meaning of sub-cl. (bb) subject to the following conditions being satisfied:
The decision of this Court is not an authority for the proposition that apart from a project or a scheme of temporary duration, S. 2(oo)(bb) of the Industrial Disputes Act will have no application.
holding: The respondent was reinstated in service with 25% back wages.
